author_or_institution: Jan Kulveit; Raymond Douglas; Nora Ammann; Deger Turan; David Krueger; David Duvenaud
title: Gradual Disempowerment: Systemic Existential Risks from Incremental AI Development
claim_or_use: Canonical full version of gradual-disempowerment argument; economy, culture, states, mutual reinforcement, incremental replacement
notes: Primary source for concept. Do not present phrase/framework as Sven Hardy Benson's invention.

author_or_institution: Jan Kulveit; Raymond Douglas; Nora Ammann; Deger Turan; David Krueger; David Duvenaud
title: Position: Humanity Faces Existential Risk from Gradual Disempowerment
claim_or_use: Peer-reviewed conference position version and concise statement of systemic-risk thesis
notes: PMLR volume 267, ICML 2025.

title: A Critique of Gradual Disempowerment
claim_or_use: Strong competing account: competent intent-aligned delegation can expand rather than reduce principal power; challenges novelty and clarity of canonical argument
notes: Treat as serious critique, not resolved fact.

title: A Defense of Gradual Disempowerment
claim_or_use: Defense emphasizing competitive pressure and effective irreversibility of delegation
notes: Attributed response to September 2026 critique.

title: Disempowerment patterns in real-world AI usage
claim_or_use: Large-scale analysis of 1.5 million Claude.ai conversations; operationalizes belief, value, and action disempowerment; severe patterns reported as rare
notes: Company-authored study of its own product; useful empirical anchor, not evidence of systemic civilizational disempowerment.

title: Monopsony Power in Labor Markets
claim_or_use: Evidence and framework for employer wage-setting power, worker outside options, search frictions, concentration and job differentiation
notes: Use to ground dependency power; review article summarizes broader literature.

author_or_institution: Erik Brynjolfsson; Danielle Li; Lindsey R. Raymond
title: Generative AI at Work
claim_or_use: Study of 5,172 customer-support agents; AI assistance increased issues resolved per hour about 15% on average with larger gains for less experienced workers
notes: Productivity evidence does not directly establish long-run employment or bargaining effects.

title: Applying AI to Rebuild Middle Class Jobs
claim_or_use: Counterargument: AI can extend expert decision capability to more workers and create human complementarities
notes: Normative possibility, not forecast.

author_or_institution: Daron Acemoglu; David Autor; Simon Johnson
title: Building Pro-Worker Artificial Intelligence
claim_or_use: Distinguishes labor-augmenting, capital-augmenting, automating, expertise-leveling and new-task-creating technologies
notes: Use as counterweight to one-directional automation thesis.

author_or_institution: Menaka Hampole; Dimitris Papanikolaou; Lawrence D. W. Schmidt; Bryan Seegmiller
title: Artificial Intelligence and the Labor Market
claim_or_use: Task-level AI exposure associated with reduced labor demand while overall employment effects at adopting firms remained modest due to productivity-driven demand
notes: Revised September 2025; do not present as final causal settlement of AI labor effects.

title: Learning from Ricardo and Thompson: Machinery and Labor in the Early Industrial Revolution, and in the Age of AI
claim_or_use: Historical and conceptual counterexample to automatic productivity-to-wage link; attention to autonomy and bargaining
notes: Use historical analogy carefully; modern AI context differs.

title: Automation and New Tasks: How Technology Displaces and Reinstates Labor
claim_or_use: Task framework separating displacement from reinstatement/new-task effects
notes: Published work exists; NBER page sufficient for research trail.

title: Automation and the Workforce: A Firm-Level View from the 2019 Annual Business Survey
claim_or_use: Large-firm adoption, higher labor productivity and lower labor shares, limited or ambiguous reported employment effects
notes: Based on 2019 Annual Business Survey; technology mix includes AI, robotics, specialized equipment/software/cloud.

title: Employment and Community: Socioeconomic Cooperation and Its Breakdown
claim_or_use: Model of employment relationships, monitoring, automation, outsourcing and community cooperation
notes: Theoretical model; use for mechanism, not prevalence claim.

title: 2023 TV/Theatrical Contracts
claim_or_use: Informed-consent and compensation provisions for specified digital-replica uses
notes: Primary union source; describe provisions rather than adopting union rhetoric as fact.

title: Artificial Intelligence
claim_or_use: 2023 MBA provisions defining AI status and interaction with covered writing work
notes: Page updated Dec. 18, 2025; primary union interpretation of contract.

title: How widespread is algorithmic management in workplaces?
claim_or_use: Cross-country employer survey on algorithmic management adoption, perceived decision quality, accountability and explainability concerns
notes: Survey covers France, Germany, Italy, Japan, Spain, United States.

title: Individual AI representatives don't solve Gradual Disempowerement
claim_or_use: Argument that individually aligned AI representatives can help while not resolving system-level disempowerment
notes: Preserve spelling of source title only in ledger; evaluate as commentary, not peer-reviewed result.

title: Gradual Disempowerment: Concrete Research Projects
claim_or_use: Candidate measurement and mitigation research directions following canonical paper
notes: Useful research agenda; not empirical validation.

title: Mitigating the Risk
claim_or_use: Authors' proposed categories of mitigation: measurement, limiting accumulation of AI influence, strengthening human control, system-wide alignment
notes: Present options and trade-offs neutrally; do not adopt policy recommendations as book verdict.
